title: subpoena-witness line
description: One line of subpoena-witness output: one exec as the kernel saw it, or a record that opens or closes a capture window. A line with a record field is a record; any other line is an exec. See docs/ports.md (W). Readers ignore fields they do not know; existing fields keep their name and meaning.

time.description: When the exec was seen, or the record written (RFC 3339, UTC).

pid.description: PID in the process's own PID namespace.

ppid.description: Parent PID in the process's own PID namespace.

host_pid.description: PID in the initial PID namespace.

comm.description: Kernel task name, at most 15 bytes.

exe.description: The path passed to execve; may be relative.

cgroup.description: cgroup path without the hierarchy root, root-most first, at most 8 elements, such as subpoena/<trace id>.

trace_id.description: The session's trace ID, read from its cgroup name. Present only for execs inside a session cgroup.

attribution.description: How the exec was tied to trace_id. Present exactly when trace_id is.

record.description: start: the witness is attached and capturing. stop: it has stopped; healthy says whether the capture between start and stop is complete.

healthy.description: On a stop record: true only if no kernel events were lost and no read or write failed.

error.description: On an unhealthy stop record: what went wrong.
